A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LatentLens work. Text and graphics support reliable comparison throughout the main paper and Appendices A–O. The additional page in v5 comes from the expanded bibliography; the appendix content matches after accounting for pagination.

before.justification: v4 reports original interpretability experiments across 15 VLM configurations, human validation of the judge, and appendix experiments including ablations, training dynamics, and caption-quality evaluation.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results, including the model comparisons in Figures 3 and 5 and the experimental results throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: The contextual-representation indexing, cross-layer cosine-neighbor retrieval, projector setup, and evolutionary phrase search in Appendix L are unchanged. Citation updates do not change the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the PixMo-Cap training and evaluation data, Visual Genome description corpus, spatial-task ablation, and rendered-text examples. No evaluated dataset, domain, or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: EmbeddingLens and LogitLens remain the main comparators. Appendix E retains Tuned Lens on the same four model pairs. The newly cited Wybitul work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The model configurations, 12K-step training with effective batch size 8, 100-patch main evaluation, GPT-5 judging procedure, and 300-image caption-quality evaluation are unchanged, as are the appendix protocols.

E4.justification: Corpus-size sensitivity, connector and training ablations, training dynamics, representation analyses, phrase-context evaluation, dynamic-corpus experiments, and qualitative case studies are all retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Seed reporting and statistical treatment are unchanged, including Appendix D's different-seed ablation and Appendix C's human-judge agreement analysis. No run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains 58.4, 67.3, 72.5, and 71.6 for the four corpus sizes, and Tables 2–6 retain their results. The new related-work sentence reports another work's finding.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, training-loss equation, similarity and top-k definitions, and Appendix E's Tuned Lens equations are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free contextual interpretation, higher interpretability than existing lenses, evaluation across 15 VLMs, and the Mid-Layer Leap finding.

C2.justification: The explanations of early semantic alignment and the Mid-Layer Leap, applicability boundaries, and limitations remain unchanged. The added Wybitul sentence supplies literature corroboration for an existing interpretation.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same code and demo links, embedding-release information, corpus construction and reservoir-sampling details, float8 storage information, runtime estimates, and comparator implementation settings.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Wybitul et al. (2026), connecting its image-optimization findings to early cross-modal alignment. Other apparent replacements, including Cunningham et al. (2023) becoming Huben et al. (2024), identify the same works with updated bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v5 adds one related-work sentence and updates numerous bibliography entries, citation labels, and the version/date stamp. The main narrative and section organization, including the appendices, remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence and longer bibliography reflow text around the conclusion and references, shifting the appendix start from page 15 to page 16. Figures and tables retain their graphics, structure, axes, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves scholarly context through the relevant Wybitul connection in Section 6 and improves reference usability through fuller publication details and links. These are limited gains; the scientific evidence, technical documentation, and limitations remain unchanged.
